key_insight: A conductive, partly crystalline GaOx hole transport layer can be formed in situ during CuInSe2 co-evaporation, enabling low-gap bottom cells with strong passivation and high voltage.
engineering_relevance: This identifies a practical back-contact/passivation strategy for 1.0 eV CuInSe2 bottom cells that supports tandem-solar integration without relying on Ag or heavy alkali additives.
method: Formed GaOx by ion exchange during co-evaporation of the absorber layer.
Tested whether Cu addition, Na, and oxygen-flow conditions affect GaOx conductivity.
Evaluated optimized cells with active-area photovoltaic performance metrics.
evidence_signal: The optimized device achieved >16% active-area efficiency and a record-certified open-circuit voltage of 552 mV.
watch_item: GaOx conductivity appears process-sensitive and partly crystalline, so reproducibility across different back contacts and deposition conditions may need careful control.
paper_title: What enables GaOx as hole transport layer for a 16 percent 1.0 eV CuInSe2 Bottom Cells with VOC above 550 mV?
